title: tidystata
text: English tidystata 把 Stata 风格的数据探索和整理带到 R 中：查看变量、汇总统计、列频数表、生成新变量。变量可以用 tidyselect 方式选择，分组计算用 .。结果都是普通的数据表，可以继续用 R 的常用工具筛选、合并和作图。

title: tidystata
code: # install.packages("pak") pak::pak("socimh/tidystata")

title: tidystata
code: library(tidystata) library(dplyr)

what: findit()：查找 Stata 命令对应的 R 代码
title: tidystata
text: 只写一个命令，例如 findit(reg)，默认显示一个明确的例子；findit(reg) |> print(n = Inf) 显示所有匹配项。可以用逗号添加变量名或提示，例如 findit(tab, sex, region) 或 findit(tab, gen)。在中文环境下运行 R 时，条目说明会显示为中文。全部条目按主题列在从 Stata 到 R中。
code: findit("reg, robust") #> # Heteroskedasticity-robust standard errors [fixest] #> Stata: regress y x1 x2, robust #> R:     fixest::feols(y ~ x1 + x2, data = data, vcov = "hetero") #> # Note: Match fixest covariance small-sample corrections and singleton handling with Stata; the same formula does not guarantee identical standard errors or retained observations. #>  #> # 17 more examples. To see them all: findit("reg, robust") |> print(n = Inf) findit("egen rowmean") #> # Average available values across columns [base] #> Stata: egen z = rowmean(x y) #> R:     data$z <- rowMeans(data[c('x','y')],na.rm=TRUE); data$z[is.nan(data$z)] <- NA_real_ #>  #> # 59 more examples. To see them all: findit("egen rowmean") |> print(n = Inf)

what: tab()、tab1() 和 tab2()：比较频数表
title: tidystata
text: 用 lifeexp 中的地区和一个新类别作比较：预期寿命是否达到 70 岁。region:lexp_70 选择这两列。 tab() 统计每种实际出现的组合的频数，并给出百分比。 tab1() 返回一个命名列表，为每个变量分别生成频数表。 tab2() 将联合频数排列成交叉表，地区为行，预期寿命类别为列。
code: lifeexp_tab <- lifeexp |>   transmute(region, lexp_70 = lexp >= 70)  tab(lifeexp_tab, region:lexp_70) #> # A tibble: 6 x 7 #>   region               lexp_70     n percent   cum valid valid_cum #>   <dbl+lbl>            <lgl>   <int>   <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl> #> 1 1 [Europe & C. Asia] FALSE      12   17.6   17.6 17.6       17.6 #> 2 1 [Europe & C. Asia] TRUE       32   47.1   64.7 47.1       64.7 #> 3 2 [North America]    FALSE       6    8.82  73.5  8.82      73.5 #> 4 2 [North America]    TRUE        8   11.8   85.3 11.8       85.3 #> 5 3 [South America]    FALSE       3    4.41  89.7  4.41      89.7 #> 6 3 [South America]    TRUE        7   10.3  100   10.3      100 tab1(lifeexp_tab, region:lexp_70) #> $region #> # A tibble: 3 x 6 #>   value                    n percent   cum valid valid_cum #>   <dbl+lbl>            <int>   <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl> #> 1 1 [Europe & C. title: tidystata
text: tidystata 还提供按行计算（row_mean() 等）、面板运算（stata_lag() 等）、相关系数（pwcorr()）、缺失值报告（misstable()）、主键检查与合并（isid()、stata_merge()）以及分组（xtile()）等函数。示例和输出约定见以下指南（英文）。 Getting started：简短的工作流程。 Containers missing values：返回类型、分组和标签。 Reference：全部函数。

title: tidystata
text: tidystata 项目遵循贡献者行为准则。参与本项目即表示你同意遵守其中的条款。

what: 在 R 中直接查询
title: 从 Stata 到 R
text: findit() 在 R 中查询同一份列表。单个 Stata 命令可以不加引号，更长的内容需要加引号；支持 Stata 的标准缩写。说明文字随 R 的语言设置显示为中文或英文，两种语言的查询都可使用。 也可以查询 R 函数（findit(left_join)），或直接提问（findit("如何删除重复行")）。 控制台显示最相关的结果，返回的表保留全部匹配项；不带参数的 findit() 返回完整列表。 逗号分隔的变量名会填入兼容的示例，例如 findit(tab, sex, region)。任务明确时默认只显示 一个优先推荐的答案；findit(tab) |> print(n = Inf) 展开全部变体、精选的 R 实现、 差异说明和参考链接。findit(dplyr::filter) 这样的包限定查询可以区分同名函数。 本指南包含 514 个命令族、181 个 Stata 函数和 3 个运算符，共有 1716 个不同的 Stata 示例和 1782 条 R 对照示例。缩写及同一任务的其他 R 实现不会增加命令数量。 R 函数索引包含 948 个函数与包的组合。
code: findit(reg) #> # Linear regression [stats] #> Stata: regress y x1 x2 #> R:     fit <- lm(y ~ x1 + x2, data = data) #> # Note: summary(fit) shows the coefficient table; broom::tidy(fit) returns it as a data frame. #>  #> # 17 more examples. To see them all: findit(reg) |> print(n = Inf) findit("merge 1:1 id, keep(match)") #> # Keep matched rows only [dplyr] #> Stata: merge 1:1 id using data2, keep(match) #> R:     inner_join(data1, data2, by = "id") #> # Note: dplyr retains overlapping non-key columns with suffixes instead of Stata master values, creates no _merge, and does not enforce a declared 1:1 key constraint. #>  #> # merge() [base]: Merge two data frames (base R) #>   Related Stata: merge #>  #> # 17 more examples. To see them all: findit("merge 1:1 id, keep(match)") |> print(n = Inf)

title: 从 Stata 到 R
text: 下表涵盖 tidystata 和其他常用 R 包，包括建模、长宽转换、调查分析和作图。 面板滞后、超前和差分可使用 tidystata 的 stata_lag()、stata_lead() 和 stata_diff()；指定时间列，并用 .区分面板。 索引按字母顺序排列，对照表按主题分组，并依次按命令、推荐顺序和示例排序。 运行某个示例需要其标注的 R 包；findit() 本身不会加载或安装这些参考包。 包标签只列出主要实现包，并不列出所有辅助依赖；R 函数索引标明其他函数及其所属包。 以 与 Stata 有差异 开头的说明表示 R 代码完成相同任务，但默认设置、缺失值处理、 估计方法或输出形式有所不同，说明会列出具体差异。其余说明是使用提示。多数 R 示例在构建目录时 运行核验，检查的是 R 代码本身，并非与 Stata 的数值一致性检验。缺失值比较、权重、因子参照组、连接规则和标准误修正尤其需要核对。 已知缺口会明确说明，相关搜索结果不代表已经实现查询中尚未支持的语法。 下表中，data 是你的数据，data1 和 data2 是合并时的主数据和被合并数据，fit 是已估计的模型。大部分条目使用 dplyr，请先用 library(dplyr) 或 library(tidyverse) 加载。 · ac · text: findit() searches list R. Type one Stata word bare, quote anything longer. Stata’s abbreviations work. can also look R function (findit(left_join)) ask question (findit("remove duplicate rows")). console shows best matches; returned table contains matches. Call findit() whole list. Descriptions follow R’s language setting; English Chinese queries work. Comma-separated names customize compatible examples, findit(tab, sex, region). default shows one preferred answer task clear; findit(tab) |> print(n = Inf) shows variants, selected alternative R approaches, qualifications source links. Package-qualified lookups findit(dplyr::filter) distinguish functions name. reference contains 514 command families, 181 Stata functions 3 operators, 1716 distinct Stata examples 1782 paired R examples. Abbreviations alternative R implementations increase command count. R index describes 948 function/package pairs.

code: library(tidystata) library(dplyr) #>  #> Attaching package: 'dplyr' #> The following objects are masked from 'package:stats': #>  #>     filter, lag #> The following objects are masked from 'package:base': #>  #>     intersect, setdiff, setequal, union  df <- data.frame(   group = c("A", "A", "B", NA),   answer = c("yes", NA, "no", "yes"),   score = c(2, NA, 6, 8) ) tbl <- tibble::as_tibble(df)  class(tab(df, answer)) #> [1] "data.frame" class(tab(tbl, answer)) #> [1] "tbl_df"     "tbl"        "data.frame" class(summ(df, score)) #> [1] "data.frame" class(summ(tbl, score)) #> [1] "tbl_df"     "tbl"        "data.frame" base_tables <- tab1(df, answer, group) class(base_tables) #> [1] "list" class(base_tables$answer) #> [1] "data.frame" class(fre(df, answer, .type = "tibble")) #> [1] "tbl_df"     "tbl"        "data.frame" if (requireNamespace("data.table", quietly = TRUE)) {   dt <- data.table::as.data.table(df)   class(tab(dt, answer))   class(summ(dt, score)) } #> [1] "data.table" "data.frame" if (requireNamespace("flextable", quietly = TRUE)) {   rich <- fre(tbl, answer, .type = "flextable")   class(rich) } #> [1] "flextable"

title: Containers, grouping and missing values
text: Summary inventory results ungrouped. Grouping keys remain ordinary columns reported. tab(), tab1(), tab2(), fre(), fre1(), fre2(), summ() tabstat(), .= NULL inherits existing groups; explicit .replaces . Cross-tabulation tab2() fre2() returns one table per group, list named group: One-way tabulations use observations within group percent cum, zero--100 scale. valid valid_cum exclude missing measured values. Missing grouping keys ordinary groups. summaries, valid_pct instead fraction zero one. summ(.missing = FALSE) removes missing grouping keys; numeric calculations always omit missing measured values.
code: grouped <- group_by(tbl, group) tab(grouped, answer) #> # A tibble: 4 × 7 #>   group answer     n percent   cum valid valid_cum #>   <chr> <chr>  <int>   <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl> #> 1 A     yes        1      50    50   100       100 #> 2 A     NA         1      50   100    NA        NA #> 3 B     no         1     100   100   100       100 #> 4 NA    yes        1     100   100   100       100 summary <- summ(grouped, score, .stat = c("n", "mean", "missing")) summary #> # A tibble: 3 × 5 #>   group type      n  mean missing #>   <chr> <chr> <int> <dbl>   <int> #> 1 A     dbl       1     2       1 #> 2 B     dbl       1     6       0 #> 3 NA    dbl       1     8       0 group_vars(summary) #> character(0) summ(grouped, score, .by = answer, .stat = c("n", "mean")) #> # A tibble: 3 × 4 #>   answer type      n  mean #>   <chr>  <chr> <int> <dbl> #> 1 no     dbl       1     6 #> 2 yes    dbl       2     5 #> 3 NA     dbl       0    NA crossed <- tab2(df, answer, score, .by = group) names(crossed) #> [1] "group = A"  "group = B"  "group = NA" tab(tbl, answer) #> # A tibble: 3 × 6 #>   answer     n percent   cum valid valid_cum #>   <chr>  <int>   <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl> #> 1 no         1      25    25  33.3      33.3 #> 2 yes        2      50    75  66.7     100   #> 3 NA         1      25   100  NA        NA summ(tbl, score, .stat = c("n", "miss_n", "valid_pct", "mean")) #> # A tibble: 1 × 5 #>   type      n miss_n valid_pct  mean #>   <chr> <int>  <int>     <dbl> <dbl> #> 1 dbl       3      1      0.75  5.33 summ(tbl, score, .by = group, .missing = FALSE, .stat = c("n", "mean")) #> # A tibble: 2 × 4 #>   group type      n  mean #>   <chr> <chr> <int> <dbl> #> 1 A     dbl       1     2 #> 2 B     dbl       1     6

title: Containers, grouping and missing values
text: ungrouped numeric column observations remains summary n = 0 NA statistics, including sum. -missing row instead row sum zero row mean NA. Empty selections give empty results tabulation; row helpers require least one column. Matrix columns supported tabulation column-summary interfaces.
code: empty <- tbl[0, ] summ(empty, score, .stat = c("n", "sum", "mean")) #> # A tibble: 1 × 4 #>   type      n   sum  mean #>   <chr> <int> <dbl> <dbl> #> 1 dbl       0    NA    NA tab1(tbl, starts_with("absent")) #> named list()  missing <- tibble(a = c(NA_real_, NA_real_), b = c(NA_real_, 4)) summ(missing, a, .stat = c("n", "sum", "mean")) #> Warning: a is entirely missing; retained with n = 0. #> # A tibble: 1 × 4 #>   type      n   sum  mean #>   <chr> <int> <dbl> <dbl> #> 1 dbl       0    NA    NA row_sum(missing) #> [1] 0 4 row_mean(missing) #> [1] NA  4

title: Containers, grouping and missing values
text: Variable labels describe columns; value labels describe particular values. Numeric calculations exclude SPSS user-missing codes Stata tagged missing values. Tabulations report missing categories alongside observed values. Summary statistics labelled numeric measurements use underlying values exclude SPSS user-missing codes. Factors use level codes warn; choose measurements deliberately instead averaging category codes. decode() displays value labels present, recode every labelled refusal ordinary NA.
code: labelled <- tibble(   response = haven::labelled_spss(     c(1, 2, 99, NA),     labels = c(Yes = 1, No = 2, Refused = 99),     na_values = 99,     label = "Interview response"   ) ) variables(labelled) #> # A tibble: 1 × 2 #>   name     label              #>   <chr>    <chr>              #> 1 response Interview response codebook(labelled) #> # A tibble: 1 × 5 #>   variable label              type             n unique #>   <chr>    <chr>              <chr>        <int>  <int> #> 1 response Interview response double+label     2      2 tab(labelled, response) #> # A tibble: 4 × 6 #>   response              n percent   cum valid valid_cum #>   <dbl+lbl>         <int>   <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl> #> 1  1 [Yes]              1      25    25    50        50 #> 2  2 [No]               1      25    50    50       100 #> 3 99 (NA) [Refused]     1      25    75    NA        NA #> 4 NA                    1      25   100    NA        NA decode(labelled$response) #> [1] "Yes"     "No"      "Refused" NA

title: Containers, grouping and missing values
text: Default list mode keeps numeric statistics numeric table. Calendar locations min, mean max formatted dates date-times, spread sd stays difftime. Table mode combines families. location column shared numeric calendar rows becomes character, spread column becomes plain number days dates seconds date-times, unit shown type column. SD uses sample denominator. Percentiles use Stata’s rule; example, quartiles 1:4 1.5 3.5. See summ() formulas, weights statistics.
code: mixed <- tibble(score = c(2, 4), day = as.Date("2024-01-01") + c(0, 2)) separate <- summ(mixed, .stat = c("n", "min", "mean", "sd", "max")) #> A list is returned as statistics are heterogeneous. names(separate) #> [1] "numeric" "date" separate$numeric #> # A tibble: 1 × 7 #>   name  type      n   min  mean    sd   max #>   <chr> <chr> <int> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> #> 1 score dbl       2     2     3  1.41     4 separate$date #> # A tibble: 1 × 7 #>   name  type      n min        mean       sd            max        #>   <chr> <chr> <int> <chr>      <chr>      <drtn>        <chr>      #> 1 day   date      2 2024-01-01 2024-01-02 1.414214 days 2024-01-03 class(separate$date$sd) #> [1] "difftime" combined <- summ(mixed, .type = "table", .stat = c("n", "min", "mean", "sd", "max")) combined #> # A tibble: 2 × 7 #>   name  type            n min        mean          sd max        #>   <chr> <chr>       <int> <chr>      <chr>      <dbl> <chr>      #> 1 score dbl             2 2          3           1.41 4          #> 2 day   date [days]     2 2024-01-01 2024-01-02  1.41 2024-01-03 class(combined$sd) #> [1] "numeric"

title: Containers, grouping and missing values
text: preview still contains 12 rows; slice contains four. n total display selection budget, split beginning end. Interval mode samples approximately evenly spaced positions; sort first position represent meaningful order. print_headtail() print_interval() print invisibly return complete input. unpreview_table() removes persistent display setting. Supported dplyr/tidyr operations carry preview settings forward following container grouping rules. Wrapping unwrapping data.table copies ; later native data.table mutations retain ordinary reference semantics.
code: long <- tibble(id = 1:12, value = (1:12)^2) preview <- preview_table(long, n = 4) preview #> # A tibble: 12 × 2 #>       id value #>    <int> <dbl> #>  1     1     1 #>  2     2     4 #> 11    11   121 #> 12    12   144 #> # ... 8 rows omitted in the middle; use print(x, n = Inf) to show all rows. nrow(preview) #> [1] 12 sum(preview$value) #> [1] 650  subset <- slice_headtail(long, n = 4) subset #> # A tibble: 4 × 2 #>      id value #>   <int> <dbl> #> 1     1     1 #> 2     2     4 #> 3    11   121 #> 4    12   144 nrow(subset) #> [1] 4 sum(subset$value) #> [1] 270 preview_table(long, style = "interval", n = 4) #> # A tibble: 12 × 2 #>       id value #>    <int> <dbl> #>  1     1     1 #>  5     5    25 #>  8     8    64 #> 12    12   144 #> # ... 8 rows omitted between displayed positions; use print(x, n = Inf) to show #> # all rows. ordinary <- unpreview_table(preview) identical(ordinary, long) #> [1] TRUE

title: Getting started with tidystata
text: codebook() gives one row per variable. variables() reports names variable labels, ds() returns character vector names. variables_search() searches names labels, can find variable description:
code: library(tidystata) library(dplyr) #>  #> Attaching package: 'dplyr' #> The following objects are masked from 'package:stats': #>  #>     filter, lag #> The following objects are masked from 'package:base': #>  #>     intersect, setdiff, setequal, union  survey <- tibble(   id = 1:6,   group = c("A", "A", "A", "B", "B", NA),   response = c("yes", "no", NA, "yes", "yes", "no"),   score1 = c(2, 4, NA, 6, 8, 10),   score2 = c(4, NA, NA, 8, 10, 12) ) attr(survey$score1, "label") <- "First assessment score"  codebook(survey) #> # A tibble: 5 × 5 #>   variable label                  type          n unique #>   <chr>    <chr>                  <chr>     <int>  <int> #> 1 id       NA                     integer       6      6 #> 2 group    NA                     character     5      2 #> 3 response NA                     character     5      2 #> 4 score1   First assessment score double        5      5 #> 5 score2   NA                     double        4      4 variables(survey) #> # A tibble: 5 × 2 #>   name     label                  #>   <chr>    <chr>                  #> 1 id       NA                     #> 2 group    NA                     #> 3 response NA                     #> 4 score1   First assessment score #> 5 score2   NA ds(survey, starts_with("score")) #> [1] "score1" "score2" variables_search(survey, "assessment") #> # A tibble: 1 × 2 #>   name   label                  #>   <chr>  <chr>                  #> 1 score1 First assessment score select_or_transmute(survey, id, starts_with("score")) #> # A tibble: 6 × 3 #>      id score1 score2 #>   <int>  <dbl>  <dbl> #> 1     1      2      4 #> 2     2      4     NA #> 3     3     NA     NA #> 4     4      6      8 #> 5     5      8     10 #> 6     6     10     12

title: Getting started with tidystata
text: counts sum six, including missing response. tab() returns observed categories counts percentages. fre() adds total rows; tab2() puts categories second variable columns. Use tab1() want separate one-way tables instead joint table: returned objects contain data. example, select categories occurring ordinary pipeline:
code: counts <- tab(survey, response) counts #> # A tibble: 3 × 6 #>   response     n percent   cum valid valid_cum #>   <chr>    <int>   <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl> #> 1 no           2    33.3  33.3    40        40 #> 2 yes          3    50    83.3    60       100 #> 3 NA           1    16.7 100      NA        NA sum(counts$n) #> [1] 6  fre(survey, response) #> # A tibble: 5 × 6 #>   response        n percent   cum valid valid_cum #>   <chr>       <int>   <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl> #> 1 no              2    33.3  33.3    40        40 #> 2 yes             3    50    83.3    60       100 #> 3 Valid Total     5    83.3  NA     100        NA #> 4 NA              1    16.7 100      NA        NA #> 5 Total           6   100    NA      NA        NA tab2(survey, group, response) #> # A tibble: 3 × 4 #>   `group \\ response`    no   yes  `NA` #>   <chr>               <int> <int> <int> #> 1 A                       1     1     1 #> 2 B                       0     2     0 #> 3 NA                      1     0     0 tables <- tab1(survey, group, response) tables$response #> # A tibble: 3 × 6 #>   value     n percent   cum valid valid_cum #>   <chr> <int>   <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl> #> 1 no        2    33.3  33.3    40        40 #> 2 yes       3    50    83.3    60       100 #> 3 NA        1    16.7 100      NA        NA tab(survey, response) |>   filter(n > 1) #> # A tibble: 2 × 6 #>   response     n percent   cum valid valid_cum #>   <chr>    <int>   <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl> #> 1 no           2    33.3  33.3    40        40 #> 2 yes          3    50    83.3    60       100

title: Getting started with tidystata
text: Select numeric measurements deliberately. Codes attached categories automatically meaningful measurements. summ() can return several statistics. tabstat() selects means default. omit missing measured values numeric calculations. Missing grouping keys remain group unless request .missing = FALSE: Numeric-summaries return table. numeric calendar measurements combined, default can list tables. companion vignette("containers--missing-values", package = "tidystata") explains types missing-value conventions.
code: summ(survey, score1, score2, .stat = c("n", "mean", "sd", "missing")) #> # A tibble: 2 × 6 #>   name   type      n  mean    sd missing #>   <chr>  <chr> <int> <dbl> <dbl>   <int> #> 1 score1 dbl       5   6    3.16       1 #> 2 score2 dbl       4   8.5  3.42       2 tabstat(survey, score1, score2, .by = group) #> # A tibble: 6 × 4 #>   group name   type   mean #>   <chr> <chr>  <chr> <dbl> #> 1 A     score1 dbl       3 #> 2 A     score2 dbl       4 #> 3 B     score1 dbl       7 #> 4 B     score2 dbl       9 #> 5 NA    score1 dbl      10 #> 6 NA    score2 dbl      12 mean(survey$score1, na.rm = TRUE) #> [1] 6 summ(survey, score1, .by = group, .missing = FALSE, .stat = c("n", "mean")) #> # A tibble: 2 × 4 #>   group type      n  mean #>   <chr> <chr> <int> <dbl> #> 1 A     dbl       2     3 #> 2 B     dbl       2     7

title: Getting started with tidystata
text: Row helpers return vectors, making convenient mutate(). pick() makes columns combined explicit. third row observed score, average NA observed count zero. Row sums use zero -missing row, column summaries use NA sum observations. Character measurements can parsed explicitly, sentinel values can replaced calculations: destring() reads numbers currency symbols, thousands separators percent signs; text, "10 kg", becomes NA warning unless remove ignore = "kg". xtile() uses Stata’s percentile cutpoints keeps tied values together; ties can leave groups empty.
code: prepared <- survey |>   mutate(     average = row_mean(pick(score1, score2)),     observed = row_non_miss(pick(score1, score2))   ) prepared #> # A tibble: 6 × 7 #>      id group response score1 score2 average observed #>   <int> <chr> <chr>     <dbl>  <dbl>   <dbl>    <int> #> 1     1 A     yes           2      4       3        2 #> 2     2 A     no            4     NA       4        1 #> 3     3 A     NA           NA     NA      NA        0 #> 4     4 B     yes           6      8       7        2 #> 5     5 B     yes           8     10       9        2 #> 6     6 NA    no           10     12      11        2 destring(c("1,200", "2,500", NA)) #> [1] 1200 2500   NA mvdecode(c(1, -99, 3), -99) #> [1]  1 NA  3 xtile(1:8, 4) #> [1] [1,2.5]   [1,2.5]   (2.5,4.5] (2.5,4.5] (4.5,6.5] (4.5,6.5] (6.5,8]   #> [8] (6.5,8]   #> Levels: [1,2.5] < (2.5,4.5] < (4.5,6.5] < (6.5,8]

title: Convert vectors for data preparation — type_conversion
text: destring() (alias as_numeric()) converts text numbers, like Stata's destring. Use mutate(x = destring(x)). decode() (alias as_character()) converts labelled vector value labels, like Stata's decode. tostring() converts values text ignores value labels, like Stata's tostring: labelled vector factor gives codes, character input returned unchanged. Missing values stay NA. Numbers written full, Stata , 100000 gives "100000", "1e+05". Dates use .character(), become "2024-01-31" rather day numbers. destring() reads text way Stata's destring . value must number, optionally sign, currency symbol (dollar, euro, pound, yen), thousands separators (1,234), trailing percent sign (50% gives 50) surrounding spaces. Anything else, "12abc", "10 kg" date, becomes NA warning, like Stata's force option; positions kept readr::problems(). Use ignore remove characters first, like Stata's ignore(): destring(x, ignore = "kg") reads "10 kg" 10. Empty strings, "NA" Stata's "." missing without warning. Dates stay NA; convert .Date() lubridate::ymd() instead. factor whose levels numbers, factor(c("1990", "2000")), gives numbers (1990, 2000). factors give level codes. Labelled numeric variables return values; labelled text read values like plain text. as_character() uses value labels labelled vector nonempty labels attribute. Without value labels, uses ordinary character conversion, including tagged missing values. SPSS user-missing codes remain values conversions. Numeric conversion preserves tagged missing values. Dates become days since 1970-01-01; date-times become seconds since Unix epoch. Durations measured vectors retain numeric values existing units. sjlabelled package also exports as_numeric() as_character(). differ: sjlabelled's as_numeric() turns non-numeric text factor codes, as_character() gives NA unlabelled values. Whichever package attached last masks ; write tidystata::as_numeric() explicit, use destring() decode(), clash.

title: Select columns with a Stata varlist — varlist
text: * matches zero characters. ~ matches one characters. ? matches one character. [-h] matches character range h. [1-12] matches number range 1 12. var1-var5 used select range variables. title: tidystata 0.3.0
text: Renamed statart tidystata, focus data exploration preparation. Legacy import/export, regression plotting wrappers removed. findit() translates Stata commands, R function names plain questions working examples, English Chinese guides. consoles colour, Stata R code retain automatic console colours. Results start compact example blocks, omit redundant function notes count remaining examples explicitly. Expanded tabulation summaries include cross-tables, weights, correlations, missing-value reports grouped calculations. Added key checks, duplicate handling, Stata-style merges, panel operators, variable transformations persistent table previews. Statistical conventions follow Stata checked output. Tables preserve input container; missing values labels handled consistently. See articles function reference details. Faster row calculations grouped aggregation, fewer required dependencies. Requires R 4.1.0 dplyr 1.1.4 later; flextable optional.
